ALEXANDER WRIGHT
alexander.wright@email.com | +1 (555) 019-2834 | San Francisco, CA | linkedin.com
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Rigorous and analytically driven Data Scientist with over 4 years of experience specializing in statistical modeling, predictive machine learning architectures, and exploratory data analysis (EDA). Proven track record of converting complex, unstructured datasets into mathematical models that solve critical predictive challenges. Expert in leveraging Python and statistical libraries to optimize algorithmic performance and deliver data-driven insight pipelines.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Statistical Analysis: Hypothesis Testing, Regression (Linear/Logistic), Bayesian Inference, Probability Distributions, ANOVA.
Machine Learning: Supervised/Unsupervised Learning, Gradient Boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM), Random Forests, Clustering (K-Means), Dimensionality Reduction (PCA).
Programming & Tools: Python (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn, SciPy), R, SQL (Advanced Querying), Git.
Data Visualization: Tableau, Seaborn, Matplotlib, Plotly.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Nexus Analytics Corp | 2024 – Present
Engineered and deployed a predictive gradient-boosted classification model using Python (Scikit-Learn) to forecast customer attrition, improving prediction accuracy by 14%.
Architected an automated data cleaning and preprocessing pipeline handling 5M+ daily unstructured data points, reducing EDA preparation time by 30%.
Designed and executed robust A/B testing frameworks, applying rigorous statistical hypothesis testing (Z-tests and T-tests) to validate algorithmic product alterations.
Developed comprehensive, interactive Tableau dashboards to visually present multi-dimensional data trends and statistical variance to executive teams.
Junior Data Analyst | Quantitative Insights Group | 2022 – 2024
Conducted deep-dive exploratory data analysis on massive historical databases using SQL and Pandas to uncover hidden variable correlations.
Built linear and logistic regression models to optimize pricing elasticity models, contributing to an algorithmic margin increase of 4%.
Maintained statistical data integrity by auditing incoming data streams for skewness, multi-collinearity, and missing value patterns.
EDUCATION
Master of Science in Applied Statistics | University of California, Berkeley
Bachelor of Science in Mathematics | Stanford University
